wa_south_face_4_the_maiden_s_escape.notes: Stored grade 5.12 PG13, 3 pitches and 91 m all match Mountain Project (300 ft); locked-1src, no change. theCrag has no Beacon entry (searched). SCOPE: Mountain Project calls it a free variation of the old, never-completed aid line Iron Maiden (A4): a new P1, the aid line's middle pitch, then a new rightward finger crack off P3 into a 5.10 corner. No Iron Maiden row exists in WA (searched name ilike maiden), so there is no parent row; it is listed as its own route and is treated as its own line here. Start: 50 ft right of the 3rd tunnel by a large oak and flat rock, old pin about 30 ft up.

wa_south_face_4_south_face.notes: IDENTIFIED, and a LIKELY DUPLICATE of wa_aging_fruits (keeper: wa_aging_fruits, the named row). The row matches Mountain Project's route titled 'South Face | 2827' (an unnamed placeholder title): 5.11- R, Trad, 65 ft (20 m), FA Avery Tichner, Summer 1985, just left of Tunnel #1 off the mossy mini-pillar shared with Fall Guy. It is NOT the historic Beacon Rock South Face/Southeast Corner line (that is wa_south_east_corner). wa_aging_fruits stores the same grade (5.11-) and the same FA ('Avery Tichner, Summer 1985'), and MP's Fall Guy page starts 'as for Aging Fruits' off the same mossy ledge and joins Aging Fruits for the spooky upper ledges to the anchor - the same finish MP's 'South Face' page describes. So both rows describe one line. Per the duplicate rule NO fixes are proposed here (not even access/permit). If the owner keeps wa_aging_fruits, the MP page could supply it pitches 1 and length 20 m (one source) plus the jill_s_thrill access/permit; batch AE held those for lack of a source. theCrag's First Tunnel sector lists neither name. SAFETY: MP says the only fixed pro is one rusty 3/8 in bolt with a homemade hanger, reached after unprotected edging; a 2018 comment says an old pin near the top is gone and calls the lead closer to X than R (a fall low down would be X-rated). The row stores no prose; the grade suffix R may understate it - owner call.
